findings.title: Vocative focus
findings.claim: The opening ya turns the brothers' report into a direct appeal to the father as the person whose decision is sought.
findings.mechanism: The vocative particle precedes the father-address after qalu, shifting the speech from reporting discovery to addressing its addressee.
findings.reader_payoff: The appeal is heard as directed persuasion before its evidence and promises are presented.
findings.containment: The finding identifies the addressee and persuasive orientation without deciding the father's response or the success of the appeal.

epistemic.reason: The claim follows the accepted word-to-QAC alignment and the local vocative attachment.

findings.title: Filial father-address
findings.claim: The form abanana makes paternal authority and filial relation audible in the collective sons' address.
findings.mechanism: The noun-of-five father form carries the first-person plural suffix, so the sons address their father while grammatically claiming the relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The appeal carries filial respect and paternal authority before the requested concessions are named.
findings.containment: The local reading remains father-address and filial relation; broader derivational pressure is kept as background and does not replace the ordinary address.

epistemic.reason: The aligned form and local grammar are secure, while the packet explicitly bounds broader root and variant pressure.

epistemic.reason: The packet support directly describes the two compatible syntactic readings and their local effect.
